_comment: Paper verdicts page -- which reviewed papers' claims SAO actually tested on SA3/SAME, and what happened. THE-FINN owns the content (add a row whenever a paper is reviewed and something is decided/run/discovered). WINTERMUTE owns the page build (build_paper_verdicts.py -> paper_verdicts.html). Sections ordered so the load-bearing content (nulled negative results, partial, confirmed) comes first; 'untested -- reviewed only' is a short reference list at the end. Each entry: id, title, link (arXiv/ACL abs url or null), claim, explanation, caveats (omit if none). Untested-section entries carry only id/title/link/claim -- no explanation/caveats prose, to keep that list scannable.

sections.title: Nulled — negative results
sections.blurb: The paper's mechanism was actually built and run on SA3/SAME, and it did not work, or made no measurable difference. These are the most informative entries on this page for anyone deciding whether to port the same idea.

entries.title: LoL: Longer than Longer, Scaling Video Generation to Hour
entries.claim: In autoregressive long-video generation with KV-cache attention sinks, head-shared RoPE causes inter-head phase concentration ("sink-collapse") at rotary phase-coherence maxima; jittering each head's RoPE base frequency (θ̂_h = θ0(1+σθ·ε_h)) de-synchronizes heads and breaks the resulting loop attractor.
entries.explanation: SAO built rope_jitter.py (per-head RoPE base-frequency jitter, citing LoL directly in its docstring) and tested it on longform.py as the team's #1 recommended long-form-coherence fix. The result was null: loopiness metric moved 0.704→0.709 (baseline 0.6707), essentially no change, reported in profiles/wintermute.journal.md 2026-07-12 ("RoPE jitter is null-by-construction on longform.py") and independently corroborated in docs/ai-research/gemini-report2-assessment-2026-07-15.md, which confirms the team tested rope_jitter and found a null on loopiness. Code-level tracing found the reason: LoL's sink-collapse requires RoPE positions to extend beyond a native window so distant frames alias onto a clamped prefix, but SA3's longform.py resets positions to 0..W every window and fifo_infinite.py uses a fixed 0..256 buffer — the aliasing condition the jitter targets never arises in SA3's bidirectional-DiT windowed regeneration, unlike LoL's autoregressive KV-cache setting.
entries.caveats: Not treated as a closed case against LoL's mechanism itself — it's flagged as an open structural-analogy question (SA3 is bidirectional-window denoising, not autoregressive with attention sinks, so the pathology may simply not transfer) rather than a refutation of LoL's claim in its own (AR) setting. A follow-up diagnostic (E3, phase-alignment) was designed to determine whether the null means "LoL's pathology isn't ours" or "our null needs a re-look inside LoL's σθ∈[0.05,0.10] band" (docs/ai-research/validation-experiment-plan-2026-07-15.md) — as of the material reviewed, E3 is still queued, not yet executed.
entries.one_liner: Hour-long video by jittering RoPE per head to break the phase re-alignment that causes long-horizon collapse.
entries.enrich: Our own rope-jitter result here is a NULL — but scoped: it was tested on windowed long-form, where positions reset per window so the RoPE-aliasing precondition never arises (that's the null's own explanation). The live testbed is the within-window loop attractor (our documented 'loops a short phrase for minutes' finding), a single forward where RoPE geometry is live — so LoL's convergence with UltraViCo is testable there without contradicting our null. The transferable ideas are the RoPE-phase-coherence diagnostic and per-head jitter; the video-AR streaming machinery does not port, and it explicitly provides no long-term memory (our prompt-arc/structure-recall gap survives).

sections.title: Partial
sections.blurb: Real experiments were run and something worked, but not the whole claim — a sub-claim held while another failed, the effect showed up on one axis but not another, or the tested version differed from the paper's exact proposal.

entries.title: Cautious Weight Decay (modded-nanogpt speedrun optimizer work)
entries.claim: Applying 'cautious' masking (only updating coordinates where the update and gradient sign agree) specifically to the weight-decay term of an optimizer improves training speed/quality without the pitfalls of masking the full update.
entries.explanation: The team ran a real cautious-optimizer A/B campaign on SA3/FusionOpt (2026-06-30 to 07-02) applying the original, broader Liang et al. 2024-style cautious masking to the FULL update — not the weight-decay-only variant this specific paper proposes — on top of a Muon/Newton-Schulz (NS5) orthogonalized optimizer path. It found a genuine, reproducible negative result: on orthogonalized paths the sign-agreement between update and raw gradient sits at keep_frac ~0.53 (barely above chance) flat across 54k steps, making cautious masking there 'a near-random ~50% sparsification' with no measured control-authority or trajectory-geometry benefit, and the standard 1/keep_frac rescale silently inflates update norm by ~1.37x, which NaN'd a rank-128 DoRA finetune (docs/findings-2026-07-02-perceptual-signal-night.md; docs/research-brief-2026-07-03-novelty-check.md). The team's own verified citation pass checked this finding against 2510.12402 and found the paper's scope is narrower (weight-decay-only caution) and does not report this failure mode: "Nobody reported our failure mechanism."
entries.caveats: The experiment does not directly test 2510.12402's actual proposal (restricting caution to weight decay) — it tests the more general/naive cautious-masking idea against an orthogonalized optimizer, and the paper's narrower design would plausibly sidestep the exact bug the team found, since weight decay itself isn't Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized. The paper functions here mainly as the closest published boundary-setter the team checked its real, negative finding against.
entries.one_liner: The closest published boundary-setter we checked our cautious-optimizer null against — its weight-decay-only caution is narrower than the full-update masking that went near-random on our orthogonalized path.
entries.enrich: Our cautious-optimizer A/B (2026-06-30 to 07-02) ran the broader Liang-2024 full-update masking, not this paper's weight-decay-only variant, on a Muon/Newton-Schulz orthogonalized path — and produced a clean negative: sign-agreement sat at keep_frac ~0.53 (near chance) flat across 54k steps, so the mask was a ~50% random sparsification with no control-authority benefit, and the standard 1/keep_frac rescale silently inflated update norm ~1.37× (which NaN'd a rank-128 DoRA run). This paper is the closest published boundary-setter we checked that against — and its narrower design plausibly sidesteps our exact bug, since weight decay itself isn't Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized. What remains ours: the orthogonalized-path failure mechanism (“nobody reported it”), the keep_frac diagnostic, and the rescale-NaN interaction.

entries.title: TADA! Tuning Audio Diffusion Models through Activation Steering
entries.claim: Activation patching reveals a small cross-attention 'semantic bottleneck' (layers {12,13}/24 in Stable Audio Open) that causally controls nearly all high-level musical concepts, and steering methods work best when confined to those layers; weight-space (LoRA) sliders confined the same way get WORSE.
entries.explanation: The team built its own causal localizer (Axis-1, layer_patch_map.py) extending TADA's activation-patching protocol from cross-attention to all three module types, and ran it on SA3 medium-base (1728 patching cells; wintermute.journal.md 2026-07-10). Result: onset density, bass weight, brightness and noisiness all localize to LATE blocks (~16-23) via self-attention and feed-forward, with cross-attention impact scores at 0.00 at every layer — the opposite shape from TADA's cross-attn-{12,13} bottleneck. However, a separate correlational strand of the team's own work lands in TADA's own territory and agrees with it: a layer x feature ridge-R2 map (docs/layer-feature-map.md) shows rhythm/onset features are 'computed' mid-stack (beat R2 peaks at L11-14), and a held-out mood-classifier probe shows categorical mood concepts peak at L8-15 — squarely inside TADA's {12,13}.
entries.caveats: TADA's own localization was measured on Stable Audio Open (acoustics-only conv-VAE) using categorical concept pairs; SAO's causal test used SA3 (semantic SAME-VAE) with continuous acoustic attributes, so the two experiments are not a strict apples-to-apples replication even where they diverge. Net picture, in the team's own words: 'different question (acoustic realization vs categorical semantics), different answer' — not a clean confirmation or a clean refutation. NB the late-block (~16-23) result is a single causal-localizer run, and the separate adapter-TRAINING-side layer-localization is still in active revision (a 2026-07-21 'write-site = compute-site' reading was overturned intraday) — so 16-23 is NOT to be read as a settled control-injection site.
entries.one_liner: The activation-patching paper whose cross-attn {12,13} 'semantic bottleneck' we extended and re-ran on SA3 — and got a different answer: control lives in late self-attn/FF, not cross-attention.
entries.enrich: We extended TADA's activation-patching protocol from cross-attention to all three module types (Axis-1, layer_patch_map.py, 1728 cells on SA3 medium-base) and got a different answer: onset density, bass weight, brightness and noisiness all localize to late blocks (~16-23) via self-attention and feed-forward, with cross-attention impact 0.00 at every layer — the opposite shape from TADA's cross-attn {12,13} bottleneck. But a correlational strand of our own work lands in TADA's territory: a ridge-R2 map puts rhythm/onset computation mid-stack (beat R2 peaks L11-14) and a held-out mood probe peaks L8-15, squarely inside {12,13}. The honest read is ‘different question (acoustic realization vs categorical semantics), different answer’ — neither a clean confirmation nor a refutation. What remains ours: the all-module causal localizer, the SAME-VAE substrate, and the late-block acoustic-attribute result.

entries.title: Stable Audio 3 (technical report — our own model)
entries.claim: Reports SA3's own architecture and training recipe: three conditioning pathways, logit-normal timestep sampling truncated at t=0.075, length-dependent timestep shift, TrackType/AudioSparx prompt-prefix convention, Muon+AdamW optimizer split, layer-14 discriminator tap, etc.
entries.explanation: Several of the paper's own claims were checked against actual model/code behavior with mixed results. (1) TrackType prefix: the paper recommends a specific prefix at inference for quality; the team discovered this prefix was missing from every one of their own captions and eval prompts, and fixed it, then ran a controlled A/B across 5 prompt-style arms (WORKLOG.md 2026-07-06/07). (2) The t<0.075-untrained crispness mechanism: initially taken at face value, then CORRECTED on 2026-07-07 after reading the actual sampler code — the truncation reshapes density, not support, so the finishing regime is thinly-trained rather than literally untrained; the crispness-late mechanism 'survives in weakened form'. (3) The layer-14 discriminator-tap hint and the init_noise_level sweet spots (0.4-0.5 timbre, 0.6 style) were both corroborated by independently-run experiments. (4) LoRA portability from base to post-trained checkpoint, stated by the repo guides, is explicitly flagged as untested.
entries.caveats: As the paper describing the team's own model, this is 'checking our own spec against our own code and outputs' rather than testing an external claim; several sub-items are confirmed while one (the untrained-region claim) required a real correction, hence 'partial' rather than a clean 'confirmed'.
entries.one_liner: Our own model's technical report — mostly confirmed against our code, but one claim (the t<0.075 'untrained' crispness mechanism) needed a real correction.
entries.enrich: Checking our own spec against our own code gave mixed results. The TrackType inference prefix the report recommends was missing from every one of our captions and eval prompts — we found it, fixed it, and A/B'd five prompt-style arms. The t<0.075 ‘untrained crispness’ mechanism we first took at face value, then corrected on 2026-07-07 after reading the sampler code: the truncation reshapes density, not support, so the finishing regime is thinly-trained, not literally untrained — the crispness effect survives in weakened form. The layer-14 discriminator tap and the init_noise sweet spots (0.4-0.5 timbre, 0.6 style) were independently corroborated; base→post-trained LoRA portability is flagged untested. What remains ours: the caption-prefix fix, the density-not-support correction, and the noise-level A/Bs.

entries.title: SHIFT: Steering Hidden Intermediates in Flow Transformers
entries.claim: A single, time-independent (temporally invariant) activation-steering vector, dual-injected into the text-encoder pooled embedding and DiT text-token activations with dynamic cosine-similarity-based per-step scaling, gives training-free concept removal/stylization control in MM-DiT flow models.
entries.explanation: The paper's headline empirical claim — that steering directions are stable across diffusion timesteps/noise levels rather than needing per-step vectors — was directly tested and replicated on SA3: diff-in-means mood-concept directions showed cross-sigma direction-cosine stability of .93-.99 across the DiT's mid-stack layers, explicitly logged as SHIFT's finding replicating on the team's own audio model (profiles/continuity.journal.md 2026-07-11). A same-day closed-loop steering render then verified training-free directional control works on SA3 (mt_dark 0.018→0.341 at alpha=+2), though that test used single-direction injection into the conditional CFG branch, not SHIFT's dual injection or its dynamic per-step scaling.
entries.caveats: Only the temporal-invariance sub-claim was tested and confirmed; the actual SHIFT mechanism (dual-hook injection with concept-presence-gated dynamic scaling, aimed at concept erasure specifically) has not been built or tested on SA3 — it remains an open item, with hook (c) flagged as needing re-derivation for SA3's separate cross-attention, unlike SHIFT's joint-attention MM-DiT target.
entries.one_liner: The closest steering paper to SA3's architecture — activation steering for the exact MM-DiT / rectified-flow family SA3 lives in, and it confirms our stable-direction result.
entries.enrich: SA3 is an MM-DiT (rectified-flow, unified attention), so SHIFT's intervention ports more directly than any LLM-steering method — it even names concrete hook points (post-shared-attention text tokens, the pooled embedding). It independently confirms our finding that the steering direction is temporally stable across generation. Its concept-presence strength-gate is a complement to our disintegration/buzz gate (orthogonal failure axes). What remains ours: the audio domain, the buzz gate, and Head-B forward-conditioning (distinct from all its inference-time readout steering).

entries.title: SaFa: Latent Swap Joint Diffusion for 2D Long-Form Latent Generation (ICCV 2025)
entries.claim: Replacing latent averaging/blending at generation-window overlaps with bidirectional latent swaps (joint denoising reconciling both windows) produces cleaner, higher-fidelity long-form joins than naive overlap-averaging.
entries.explanation: The team built a direct A/B comparing a frame-interleave latent-SWAP join against their existing slerp/averaging bridge for SA3 longform window stitching, targeting the RMS/HF-variance collapse mechanism SaFa's paper identifies. Result (2026-07-13): swap join holds seam HF-variance at 1.159x versus slerp's suppression to 0.818x, with RMS ratio ~1.0 in both arms — confirming the paper's mechanism (averaging specifically suppresses high-frequency variance at seams, not overall energy). A same-day co-score found the swap join's loopiness metric identical to slerp's, 0.680 = 0.680 — the join method does not touch the loop-repetition failure mode at all. Team verdict, stated explicitly: "SaFa's win is REAL but NARROW" — confirmed on the seam-HF-variance axis, null on the loopiness axis.
entries.caveats: This tested only SaFa's core swap-join operator via a join-level frame-interleave approximation, not the paper's full per-step joint-diffusion sequential renderer — an upgrade to the exact algorithm is a pending pool item. The paper's second operator (Reference-Guided Latent Swap, for cross-window timbre/acoustic drift) was separately identified as never having been ported, so that half of SaFa remains genuinely untested on SA3.
entries.one_liner: Seamless long-form by swapping (not averaging) overlapping windows — a training-free alternative to the per-window seams SA3 currently generates.
entries.enrich: This is exactly the seam mechanism SA3 lacks: seams come from blending overlaps, and a hard swap over jointly-denoised windows removes them — whereas SA3 resets the clock per window and generates windows independently. Its reference-guided swap is a consistency-without-repetition knob for loop-collapse, and it's MM-DiT-validated while touching no attention/RoPE. The caveat is the paper's own: it's 2D-mel + DDPM; our 1D-SAME + rectified-flow are the untested cases, so whether the swap operator survives RF trajectories must be checked first.

entries.title: Physics-aware auxiliary losses (states a redundancy condition near-verbatim, discriminative GNN setting)
entries.claim: In a discriminative GNN setting, a redundant auxiliary loss (one carrying no information beyond the main task) is neutral rather than harmful.
entries.explanation: Cited, not independently fetched (no local PDF), but this is a genuine comparison against the team's own tested finding. knowledge.md: "Finds redundant aux NEUTRAL, not harmful — our generative-manifold degradation goes beyond it." The team's own finding (a redundant auxiliary loss — the genre-consistency probe — is actively harmful in their generative-manifold setting) goes further than / partially contradicts this paper's finding in a different problem setting.
entries.caveats: Not a like-for-like replication (discriminative GNN vs. generative rectified-flow manifold) — worded here as 'partial / nulled-in-a-different-domain' rather than a direct refutation.
entries.one_liner: Finds a redundant auxiliary loss neutral in a discriminative GNN — our generative-manifold result goes further: a redundant-but-confining aux is actively harmful.
entries.enrich: This is a citation-level comparison (no local PDF), but a real one: the paper finds a redundant auxiliary loss neutral in a discriminative GNN, and our own tested finding goes further — a redundant aux (the genre-consistency probe) is actively harmful in our generative rectified-flow manifold, dragging steering 0.92→0.65. Different problem setting (discriminative vs generative), so it reads as ‘nulled in a different domain’ rather than a head-on refutation. What remains ours: the generative-manifold harm mechanism, which this paper's discriminative setting cannot exhibit.

entries.title: InfiniteAudio: Infinite-Length Audio Generation with Consistent Acoustic Attributes
entries.claim: A FIFO/'diagonal denoising' scheme (staggered per-frame noise levels, rolling the denoising window forward frame-by-frame), with a buffer zone specifically to keep per-frame noise in-distribution, enables infinite-length generation with consistent acoustic attributes on scalar-noise-conditioned audio latent diffusion models -- training-free, per the paper's own abstract.
entries.explanation: The team ported this method to SA3 (WORKLOG.md 2026-06-18: "Ported InfiniteAudio (arXiv:2506.03020) long-form / FIFO diagonal denoising to SA3"), requiring real model surgery since SA3's DiT only accepts a scalar-per-batch timestep and had to be monkeypatched to accept per-token (B,T) sigmas. When GPU-validated (WORKLOG.md 2026-06-21), the FIFO prototype 'cratered to ~0.03 at ~18s' on the drift/RMS metric, versus a competing sliding-window inpaint-continuation approach that stayed flat ([1.03, 0.95, 0.75, 0.83, 1.04]). Tracing the port found the port had disabled the paper's own buffer-zone safeguard (the mechanism the paper itself uses to keep per-frame noise in-distribution) -- so the observed failure reflects an incomplete port of the method, not a test of the paper's method as actually proposed.
entries.caveats: This is NOT a rejection of the paper's claim: the paper is an audio paper (KAIST/Interspeech, AudioLDM-class scalar-noise-conditioned model) proposing exactly the class of model SA3 belongs to, and its abstract states the method is training-free on such models -- both facts this entry previously mischaracterized (an earlier draft wrongly called it a video-DiT per-frame-noise-training method). The honest verdict is partial: our port dropped the paper's own OOD guard and then observed the exact failure that guard exists to prevent; a corrected port (with the buffer zone intact) has not yet been tried. The team kept the FIFO code as a future 'Approach C' engine for exactly this reason.
entries.one_liner: Training-free infinite-length audio via a rolling diagonal-noise buffer — continuous context, no window seam.
entries.enrich: Its FIFO rolling diagonal-noise buffer is a seamless alternative to our reset-the-clock-per-window scheme — the seam is exactly where loop-collapse lives. It's training-free and testable on SA3 as-is, but DDPM-on-mel, so the per-frame timestep needs remapping onto the rectified-flow time variable. Its self-attention-map diagnostic is worth running on SA3 to test the over-attends-a-fixed-region hypothesis for loop-collapse. What remains ours: the RF/SAME domain, the buzz gate, and the conditioning arc it complements.

entries.title: Analyzing and Improving the Training Dynamics of Diffusion Models (EDM2)
entries.claim: Section 3 proposes post-hoc power-function EMA: logging two power-EMA snapshots during training lets you reconstruct the optimal EMA length for any checkpoint after the fact, rather than fixing an EMA length in advance — and the optimal length is claimed to depend on the sampling configuration (e.g. CFG strength) rather than being a fixed training-time constant.
entries.explanation: Tested on SA3 via the temporal-soup campaign (the team's own C1/C2 experiments): checkpoint-averaging (soups) was compared against terminal (un-averaged) checkpoints across several training ladders, and averaging won — a real, standing confirmation of EDM2's core premise that a good weight average beats a single late checkpoint. The paper's more specific implication — that no single global averaging profile should dominate, since the optimal one varies per run/config — also came out confirmed, but in a nuanced rather than clean-cut form: a mechanical PQ×crest×whitening quality-weighted soup was built as a candidate 'smarter than uniform' profile, and it was competitive with plain uniform/exponential averaging but did not consistently beat it across ladders — sometimes winning one axis (perceptual quality) while losing another (dynamic range), exactly the per-run variation EDM2's argument predicts rather than a universal winner.
entries.caveats: The by-ear listening pass on the quality-weighted soups vs uniform ones was still pending as of this entry — the metrics wash does not settle whether one sounds better, only that neither dominates on the measured axes. The paper's own optimal-EMA-length-varies-with-CFG claim (their Fig. 6, no-CFG ~13% vs cfg-1.4 ~2%) has not yet been tested directly on SA3's own cfg7/cfg16 operating points.
entries.one_liner: The paper behind our checkpoint-soup campaign: averaging beats a single terminal checkpoint, confirmed — but a fancier quality-weighted average didn't clearly beat plain uniform averaging either, which is itself consistent with the paper's own per-run-varies argument.
entries.enrich: Our temporal-soup campaign (C1/C2) confirmed EDM2's core claim — averaging beats a terminal checkpoint — across several training ladders. We then built the paper's more specific implication into a real test: a PQ×crest×whitening quality-weighted average, meant to beat plain uniform averaging the way EDM2 predicts a well-chosen profile should. It didn't consistently win — competitive, sometimes ahead on one axis and behind on another, never a clean sweep. That is itself the nuanced confirmation: no single averaging profile dominates, exactly EDM2's own point, just not yet resolved by ear. What remains ours: the quality-weighting formula, the per-ladder comparison, and the open listening pass.

entries.title: On the Mismatch Between Adam-Pretrained Models and Muon Fine-tuning
entries.claim: Fine-tuning an Adam-pretrained base model with a Muon-family (orthogonalized-update) optimizer is a documented mismatch case: because the base's weight spectrum was never shaped by an orthogonalized update, Muon fine-tuning shows more forgetting and is hypersensitive to update strength compared to matched Adam fine-tuning.
entries.explanation: The optimizer-shape concern was confirmed directly on our own substrate by a step-resolution trajectory-sketch campaign, not just cited as a plausible warning: constant-LR AdamW at small effective batch measures as a pure random walk on the weight trajectory (update autocorrelation decays as 0.9^τ then hits exactly zero; gradient window-SNR sits at the 1/w noise floor out to w=1024; zero net drift over 10,000 steps), while our production optimizer (Fusion, a Newton-Schulz/Muon-family orthogonalizing update) shows real, non-vanishing drift on the identical data (autocorrelation 0.215 at τ=100, versus AdamW's exact zero) — a directly measured instance of exactly the base-was-never-orthogonalized-shaped mismatch this paper warns about.
entries.caveats: Mechanism confirmed; the paper's prescribed remedy (a matched, properly-tuned Adam fine-tune as the fair comparison) is still in flight as a dedicated full-fine-tune control campaign, not yet landed — so whether Muon fine-tuning is actually WORSE in outcome (not just different in trajectory shape) on our substrate remains open. Row as partial, not confirmed, until those control arms report.
entries.one_liner: Predicted our AdamW-vs-Fusion trajectory split before we measured it: AdamW walks randomly on our base, Fusion (Muon-family) drifts — exactly the orthogonalized-update mismatch this paper describes. The remedy arms (a fair matched-Adam control) are still running.
entries.enrich: A step-resolution trajectory recorder let us watch the mismatch this paper describes happen in real time on our own base model: constant-LR AdamW at small batch is statistically indistinguishable from a random walk (autocorrelation collapses to exactly zero, gradient signal sits at the noise floor, no net drift over 10k steps), while our production Muon-family optimizer shows real, measurable drift on the identical data. That is the mechanism the paper warns about, directly measured rather than inferred. What remains open, and ours to close: whether that trajectory difference actually translates into a worse fine-tuned model, which needs the matched-Adam control arms this finding motivated — those are running, not yet verdicted.

sections.title: Confirmed
sections.blurb: The paper's claim was tested (directly, or via a deliberately cheaper/adapted version of its method) and held up on SA3/SAME's own evidence.

entries.title: Discovering and Steering Interpretable Concepts in Large Generative Music Models
entries.claim: Sparse autoencoders trained on a music generator's residual stream discover human-interpretable concepts, and simple activation-addition (adding a decoder direction) steers generation toward those concepts for a meaningful (15-35%) fraction of features, audibly to listeners.
entries.explanation: The team explicitly skipped the SAE-training step (citing AxBench's finding that supervised directions beat SAE features for LLMs) and instead ran the cheaper, paper-inspired experiment directly: diff-in-means concept directions computed from labeled MIR/mood features on SA3's own DiT activation dumps, injected at mid/late blocks via conditional-branch-only activation addition. Phase 3 landed the same day: mt_dark steered Essentia dark score 0.018 → 0.341 at alpha=+2 (19x, zero training); mt_uplifting steered only in the negative direction; mt_relaxing was dead — summarized in-journal as '1 clean + 1 partial of 3 moods ~ the MusicGen paper's 15-35% steerable fraction; "select the right features" holds' (profiles/continuity.journal.md, 2026-07-11). Cross-sigma direction stability of .93-.99 was also measured in the same run.
entries.caveats: This is a training-free activation-addition experiment on SA3's DiT residual stream using supervised (diff-in-means) directions rather than SAE-discovered ones, so it tests the paper's steering claim and steerable-fraction finding, not its SAE-discovery pipeline itself; the paper's own abstract file already anticipated this as the 'cheap follow-up' before it was run.
entries.one_liner: The MusicGen-SAE steering paper we followed the cheap way — supervised diff-in-means directions on SA3, landing the same ~15-35% steerable fraction it reports, at zero training cost.
entries.enrich: We skipped the SAE-training step (on AxBench's finding that supervised directions beat SAE features) and ran the cheaper, paper-inspired experiment: diff-in-means concept directions from labeled MIR/mood features on SA3's DiT activations, injected conditional-branch-only at mid/late blocks. Phase 3 (2026-07-11): mt_dark steered Essentia dark 0.018→0.341 at α=+2 (19×, zero training), mt_uplifting steered one-directionally, mt_relaxing was dead — ‘1 clean + 1 partial of 3 moods’, right on the paper's 15-35% steerable fraction, with cross-σ direction stability .93-.99. What remains ours: the training-free diff-in-means shortcut, the conditional-branch-only injection, and the audio domain (the paper is MusicGen).

entries.title: SAME: A Semantically-Aligned Music Autoencoder (our own latent space)
entries.claim: SAME's soft-normalization latent bottleneck (not a VAE) has semantics trained in via a joint flow-matching alignment loss, linear chroma/ILD regressors, and contrastive text alignment, producing a decode-robust, linearly-decodable, text-aligned latent space.
entries.explanation: One of SAME's specific design goals was tested directly: linear decodability. The team's own layer x feature ridge-R2 map found several acoustic features (spectral flux/flatness/skewness -- a related linear-probe test on the same latent space, not literally SAME's own chroma/ILD regressor targets) already near-ceiling R2 (0.86-0.94) at layer 0 of the DiT -- consistent with, though not a direct replication of, SAME's linear-decodability design goal. Separately, the team's OWN reasoning (papers/knowledge.md, NOT a caution stated in the SAME paper itself, which contains no discussion of TADA or cross-attention localization) held that SA3's semantic bottleneck might sit elsewhere than TADA's Stable-Audio-Open-derived {12,13}, specifically because SAME trains semantics in differently than Stable Audio Open's acoustics-only conv-VAE. This team-authored hypothesis was tested via the Axis-1 causal localizer (see the TADA! entry above), which found SA3's acoustic-attribute localization is indeed NOT at cross-attn {12,13} but at late self-attn/FF blocks -- consistent with the hypothesis.
entries.caveats: Corrected from an earlier draft that wrongly attributed the TADA-transfer caution to the SAME paper itself -- it is the team's own reasoning, informed by SAME's design, not a claim the paper makes. The localizer test is the same experiment cited under the TADA! entry; it confirms the CAUTION (don't assume the same bottleneck location transfers) rather than pinning down where SAME's own semantic bottleneck specifically lives.
entries.one_liner: Our own semantically-aligned latent — its linear-decodability design goal shows up directly in our layer-0 ridge-R2 map.
entries.enrich: We tested one of SAME's specific design goals directly — linear decodability. Our layer×feature ridge-R2 map found several acoustic features (flux/flatness/skewness) already near-ceiling R2 0.86-0.94 at DiT layer 0, consistent with SAME's linear-decodability design (a related probe, not literally SAME's own chroma/ILD regressor targets). Our own reasoning — informed by SAME training semantics in differently than an acoustics-only conv-VAE — predicted SA3's semantic bottleneck would not sit at TADA's {12,13}; the Axis-1 localizer confirmed exactly that (late self-attn/FF, not cross-attn {12,13}). What remains ours: the layer-0 linear-decodability evidence and the where-is-the-bottleneck hypothesis SAME's design motivated (the paper itself discusses neither TADA nor localization).

entries.title: Applying Guidance in a Limited Interval Improves Sample and Distribution Quality in Diffusion Models (Kynkäänniemi et al., NeurIPS 2024)
entries.claim: Classifier-free guidance should only be applied within a limited interval of noise levels (sigma range), not across the whole sampling trajectory, to improve sample/distribution quality; CFG applied broadly is most mode-collapsing in the mid-noise band.
entries.explanation: SA3's own DiT INHERITS sigma-gated limited-interval guidance from its upstream codebase (dit.py:479) -- this is not something the team implemented from the paper, and the gate ships OFF BY DEFAULT (cfg_interval=(0,1), i.e. guidance applied everywhere unless explicitly narrowed). The team's own explorer UI iteration (2026-07-08) surfaced the existing control in a sigma-schedule chart with a range-slider cfg_interval control, described in chat as SA3's 'native limited-interval guidance (DiT sigma-gated, Kynkaanniemi 2024)' (AGENT_DIALOGUE.md, 2026-07-08). Separately, WINTERMUTE's melodic_movement_ladder measurement found a real U-shaped mode-collapse in a2a chroma-flux/pc-transition metrics that bottoms in the mid-noise band (nl .40-.55, -20% vs source) -- consistent with, but not an isolated test of, the paper's mid-band CFG-collapse claim: the team's own note co-cites this U-shape to THREE mechanisms at once (SDEdit projection regime, Kynkaanniemi's interval-CFG collapse, and EDM deterministic-sampling basin-trapping), so it's a confounded real-world observation consistent with the paper, not a clean replication isolating its specific mechanism.
entries.caveats: The mechanism is inherited from upstream, ships disabled by default, and the paper's own headline claim (limiting the interval IMPROVES quality) has never been directly A/B'd by the team -- what's confirmed is that the knob exists, works, and that a real measurement is consistent with (one of three plausible explanations for) the paper's predicted failure mode, not a controlled test of the claim itself. A follow-up controlled A/B (interval-limited CFG vs. chroma-guided steering in the mid-band) was proposed but not yet reported as run.
entries.one_liner: Limited-interval CFG — a knob SA3 already inherits (sigma-gated, off by default); our mid-band mode-collapse measurement is consistent with the failure mode it predicts.
entries.enrich: SA3's DiT already inherits sigma-gated limited-interval guidance from upstream (dit.py:479), shipping OFF by default (cfg_interval=(0,1)). We surfaced the existing control in the explorer UI (2026-07-08) as a sigma-schedule range-slider, and WINTERMUTE's melodic_movement_ladder found a real U-shaped mode-collapse bottoming in the mid-noise band (nl .40-.55, -20% vs source) — consistent with the paper's mid-band CFG-collapse claim. Honest caveat: we co-cite that U-shape to three mechanisms at once (SDEdit projection, interval-CFG collapse, EDM basin-trapping), so it's a confounded real observation, not an isolated test — and the paper's headline (limiting the interval improves quality) has never been directly A/B'd. What remains ours: confirming the knob exists and works, and the (confounded) mid-band collapse measurement.

entries.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs, Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
entries.claim: On a systematic LLM steering benchmark, simple supervised baselines (e.g. difference-in-means / linear probes) outperform Sparse Autoencoder (SAE)-based steering methods.
entries.explanation: The team explicitly invoked AxBench's finding as the reason to skip building an SAE steering pipeline for SA3 and go straight to a supervised diff-in-means approach (AGENT_DIALOGUE.md, 2026-07-11). They then built and ran exactly that simple baseline on SA3's DiT activations and it worked well: mood concepts separated cleanly at L8-15 with split-half held-out AUCs of .69-.93, and Phase 3 injection produced real, audible, closed-loop-verified steering on SA3 (mt_dark 0.018→0.341 at alpha=+2). No SAE arm was ever separately trained and benchmarked head-to-head on SA3, so this is confirmation-by-application (the simple baseline AxBench recommends was sufficient and successful) rather than a controlled SAE-vs-diff-in-means bake-off on the team's own stack.
entries.caveats: Not a true head-to-head replication — the team never built a comparison SAE steering baseline on SA3 to test against; they took AxBench's finding on faith and it paid off. A 2026-07-13 summary listing 'SAE-vs-supervised' among the week's research-verification wins somewhat overstates the rigor of what was actually a one-arm application, not a comparison.
entries.one_liner: The benchmark that says simple difference-of-means beats sparse autoencoders for steering — a result we already acted on.
entries.enrich: This is the paper our 2026-07-12 mood-steering acted on — we skipped SAE training and used difference-of-means, which delivered ~19x 'dark' steering on a closed-loop meter. Three of its findings replicated on SA3: detection ≠ steering (our 'relaxing' mood had the best separability yet refused to steer), big vectors harm quality (now our disintegration gate), and SAEs underperform (which bounds our SAE-steering lane). Its ReFT-r1 (rank-1 joint finetune) is a candidate worth testing against our readout heads. What remains ours: the audio domain, the buzz gate they lack, and Head-B forward-conditioning.

sections.title: Independent convergence
sections.blurb: The team built the same mechanism the paper describes before finding (or independently of finding) the paper itself, typically discovered afterward during a deliberate novelty/prior-art check.

entries.title: ControlNet++: Improving Conditional Controls with Efficient Consistency Feedback
entries.claim: Controllable diffusion adapters can be trained with a cycle-consistency loss: noise the input, take a one-step denoised estimate, score it with a frozen off-the-shelf discriminative 'meter', and back-propagate a t-gated (low-noise-only) consistency loss into the adapter, instead of relying only on the base diffusion loss.
entries.explanation: The team built 'FusionCC' — a loss that decodes a one-step denoised latent estimate (rf_z0_hat), scores it with a frozen probe, and back-propagates a timestep-gated consistency loss into an adapter — and only discovered ControlNet++ afterward during a deliberate novelty/prior-art check. The team's own verified citation pass states it plainly: "mechanism-identical to FusionCC — the prior-art call stands, no wiggle room" (docs/research-brief-2026-07-03-novelty-check.md; AGENT_DIALOGUE.md 2026-07-03). FusionCC's onset-density variant trained 2026-07-02 and posted the campaign's first statistically significant win (corr .584→.880 at gain 2, bootstrap CI excludes zero; re-confirmed on a corrected onset meter). A companion run applying the same recipe to a genre-consistency probe (a global, RF-visible property) actively hurt steering (0.92→0.65), giving the team a boundary condition — 'the meter must carry information the training loss doesn't already have' — that the ControlNet++ line does not state.
entries.caveats: The paper's own t-gate scales window width with how 'global' the metered property is (edges 200 vs depth 400 out of 1000); the team's boundary condition (blind-vs-redundant) and the genre negative control are noted internally as the unpublished addition on top of the reinvented mechanism, not a criticism of the paper.
entries.one_liner: We built its exact cycle-consistency mechanism as 'FusionCC' before we found the paper — mechanism-identical, and the source of our first statistically-significant control win.
entries.enrich: We built the exact mechanism — ‘FusionCC’, decoding a one-step z0-hat estimate, scoring it with a frozen probe, back-propagating a timestep-gated consistency loss — and only found ControlNet++ afterward in a novelty check (‘mechanism-identical, no wiggle room’). FusionCC's onset-density variant posted the campaign's first significant win (corr .584→.880 at gain 2, bootstrap CI excludes zero). A companion run on a genre-consistency probe actively hurt steering (0.92→0.65), giving us a boundary condition the ControlNet++ line doesn't state: the meter must carry information the training loss doesn't already have. What remains ours: the blind-vs-redundant boundary condition and the genre negative control.

entries.title: InnerControl ("Heeding the Inner Voice"): all-timestep alignment via t-conditioned probes on intermediate diffusion features
entries.claim: Cycle-consistency control losses that only work on clean (low-noise) latent estimates fail when extended naively to noisy/early timesteps (alignment improves but quality craters); the fix is to train lightweight t-conditioned probes directly on noisy intermediate features so the alignment signal can be applied across nearly the whole denoising trajectory.
entries.explanation: SA3's LatCH ('Latent-Control Heads') already implement t-conditioned probes via a t_injection mechanism, built no later than 2026-05-29 (stable-audio-3 fork, commit 28de3ee, 'adaln_zero t-injection + TimeConditioningCache for SA3 LatCH') — over a month before the team's deep-read of InnerControl on 2026-07-03. After the deep-read, the team explicitly designed a direct application — 'FusionCC v1.3': replacing FusionCC's clean-z0 probe with a t-conditioned meter on noised latents for all-timestep supervision (WORKLOG.md 2026-07-03). That extension was deliberately deferred, not run: "designed, deliberately deferred, not lost…parked because the plain-CC scope condition needed validating first" (docs/onset-density-control-narrative.md).
entries.caveats: Two distinct things map onto this paper: (1) LatCH's pre-existing t-conditioned-probe ARCHITECTURE is a genuine independent convergence on the paper's core representational idea, predating the paper's discovery -- but only the architecture converges, not the paper's full all-timestep TRAINING scheme, which the team never built at LatCH's original design time; (2) the direct, paper-inspired extension of FusionCC to an all-timestep t-conditioned probe (FusionCC v1.3) was designed but never trained -- a declined/deferred experiment with a stated reason, not a run one.
entries.one_liner: Its all-timestep t-conditioned-probe idea is one our LatCH heads already implemented a month before we read it — an architecture convergence (the full training scheme we designed but deferred).
entries.enrich: Two things map onto this paper. Our LatCH heads already implemented its core idea — t-conditioned probes on noisy intermediate features (via t_injection, commit 28de3ee, no later than 2026-05-29) — over a month before we deep-read InnerControl, a genuine architecture-level convergence. After the read we designed the direct extension (FusionCC v1.3: swap the clean-z0 probe for a t-conditioned meter for all-timestep supervision) but deliberately deferred training it until the plain-CC scope condition was validated. What remains ours: the pre-existing t-conditioned LatCH architecture (the convergence), and the honest fact that the full all-timestep training scheme is designed-but-not-run.

entries.title: Optimizer-Induced Low-Dimensional Drift and Transverse Dynamics ("Backbone" trajectory-PCA)
entries.claim: 60-80% of optimizer displacement during training concentrates in a low-dimensional subspace under uncentered PCA, attributed to optimizer-induced structure.
entries.explanation: The team ran its own checkpoint-trajectory PCA on a ~120M-parameter adapter fine-tune (10 checkpoints, Gram-trick PCA validated against a random-walk null) during the 2026-07-01/02 'perceptual-signal night' and found top-2 explained variance 0.969 vs 0.776 for the null, with 88% of weight motion in PC1 and a PC2 arc that turns over near epoch 5 — coinciding with the checkpoint-averaging centroid and Kim's independent audition sweet spot. The 2602.23696 paper was only surfaced afterward, during a 2026-07-03 novelty/citation check, as the nearest piece of prior art — the team had not read it before running its own PCA. On comparison the two findings differ in kind, not just degree: 2602.23696 uses uncentered PCA on raw displacement (60-80%); the team's is centered PCA on variance (88%, a stronger planarity statement) plus a PC2-turnover signal functioning as a loss-blind early-stopping proxy, which the paper does not report.
entries.caveats: This is prior-art discovered after independent derivation, not a test of the paper's specific claim — the team did not re-run an uncentered-PCA analysis to check whether the paper's own 60-80% figure holds on their stack; the comparison is at the level of method and interpretation, not a replication.
entries.one_liner: Low-dimensional optimizer drift — we independently ran the same checkpoint-trajectory PCA (88% of motion in PC1) before surfacing this as the nearest prior art.
entries.enrich: We ran our own checkpoint-trajectory PCA on a ~120M-param adapter fine-tune (10 checkpoints, Gram-trick, validated against a random-walk null) during ‘perceptual-signal night’ — top-2 EV 0.969 vs 0.776 null, 88% of weight motion in PC1, and a PC2 arc turning over near epoch 5 that coincided with the checkpoint-averaging centroid and Kim's independent audition sweet spot. We surfaced 2602.23696 only afterward as nearest prior art. The findings differ in kind: they use uncentered PCA on raw displacement (60-80%); ours is centered PCA on variance (88%, a stronger planarity statement) plus a PC2-turnover early-stopping proxy the paper doesn't report. What remains ours: the centered-variance formulation and the loss-blind PC2-turnover stopping signal.

entries.title: Audio-to-Audio via Diffusion Warm Initialization
entries.claim: SDEdit-style warm-start diffusion has an empirically locatable skip-fraction sweet spot (found via a pitch-Jaccard-Distance + FAD metric sweep on Stable Audio Open), and re-adding noise to the guide (lambda=1) is usually unnecessary/can hurt versus treating the guide as already on the intermediate marginal (lambda=0).
entries.explanation: SAO's Longform feature already ships the identical mechanism — a whole-segment SDEdit re-anchor (SDEditReanchor in stable_audio_3/inference/longform.py) — and it was built and merged on 2026-06-19/2026-06-21, contemporaneous with or predating this paper's public posting; the team built the SDEdit-re-anchor idea on their own rather than adopting it from this paper. The sourcebook's 2026-07-06 revisit explicitly notes 'the mechanism is precisely Longform's already-shipped SDEdit re-anchor… No new capability here' and flags the paper's lambda=0-vs-1 finding as 'a mild confirmation of standard SDEdit practice, not a new finding for anyone who has already implemented and shipped this mechanism.'
entries.caveats: The paper's proposed JD+FAD metric-sweep tuning-harness pattern was explicitly noted as possibly useful ('worth a line…if re-anchor timestep selection is ever revisited') but a search of the logs turns up no evidence it was actually adopted — Longform's re-anchor timestep remains hand-set, not metric-swept, as far as the record shows.
entries.one_liner: An SDEdit skip-fraction sweet spot — a mechanism our Longform re-anchor already ships; the paper reads as mild confirmation, not a new capability.
entries.enrich: SAO's Longform feature already ships the identical mechanism — a whole-segment SDEdit re-anchor (SDEditReanchor in longform.py), built 2026-06-19/21, contemporaneous with or predating this paper. Our 2026-07-06 revisit notes ‘the mechanism is precisely Longform's already-shipped SDEdit re-anchor… no new capability here’, and reads the paper's λ=0-vs-1 finding as mild confirmation of standard SDEdit practice. Its JD+FAD metric-sweep tuning harness was flagged as possibly-useful-if-revisited, but the logs show Longform's re-anchor timestep is still hand-set, not metric-swept. What remains ours: the shipped re-anchor itself; the metric-swept timestep selection is the one thing we could still borrow.

entries.title: Low-Resource Guidance for Controllable Latent Audio Diffusion ("LatCH" source paper)
entries.claim: Training-free guidance (TFG-style rho/mu variance/mean guidance, gamma noise-convolution, n_iter mean-guidance iterations) using small MIR-feature prediction heads on noisy latents can steer a frozen latent audio diffusion model toward requested control targets without retraining the base model.
entries.explanation: The team's own LatCH guidance-head infrastructure (docs/latch.md; latch_guided.py with exactly the paper's rho/mu/gamma/n_iter TFG parameterization) was built and iterated starting no later than 2026-05-31, and was ported to SA3 through June-July 2026 (onset head steering 2026-06-23, chroma/beat/hardness heads through 07-10). The team only recognized this exact paper as the method's source on 2026-07-15, via a cross-check: "LatCH 2603.04366 is REAL, ICASSP 2026, authors = THE STABLE AUDIO TEAM…our latch infra implements it per LATCH_README." A follow-up read of the full paper confirmed the TFG design space (rho/mu, gamma, n_iter, selective step windows, multi-guide weighting) is fully ported and working on SA3.
entries.caveats: This is a genuine independent-convergence case, not a validated port: the team built the mechanism first and discovered the paper as prior art afterward. Three paper components were explicitly identified as NOT yet ported/tested: LatCH-B (backwards-simulated/rollout-trained heads), the sparsity-aware loss for high-dimensional sparse targets, and N_recur time-travel recurrence — these remain untested future work, not confirmed-working replications.
entries.one_liner: The Stability/SAO paper that coined 'LatCH' — but here it means a guidance readout head, not our conditioning adapter (a term to reconcile).
entries.enrich: This is the origin of the name 'LatCH' — and it means something different here: a guidance readout head (predict a control feature, take a distance-gradient), not our training-time conditioning adapter; the term needs reconciling before porting claims. Its finding that 1D low-frequency controls (RMS/onset) work while sparse high-dim ones (pitch/chroma) fail directly constrains our adapter targets — and gets worse at our coarser 10.77 Hz latent, independently predicting our Head-A pitch ceiling. Its guidance math is DDIM/score-based, so it needs re-deriving for rectified flow. What remains ours: the RF/SAME domain and the buzz gate.

entries.title: TAC-GAN (AC-GAN outputs confined by frozen auxiliary classifier decision boundaries)
entries.claim: An auxiliary discriminative classifier's decision boundary can be used to confine/steer generative outputs, without redundancy conditioning.
entries.explanation: Cited, not independently fetched (no local PDF). knowledge.md: "the HARM mechanism of our boundary condition, formalized — but with no redundancy conditioning." Independent-convergence-flavored: the team found this mechanism themselves (the manifold-confinement harm behind their genre-consistency negative result); this paper names/formalizes half of it, and was surfaced as prior art rather than a source the team built from.
entries.caveats: No PDF fetched; the citation is used only for the boundary-condition writeup, not as a tested-against comparison in its own right.
entries.one_liner: Formalizes half of our boundary condition — an auxiliary classifier's decision boundary confining generation — the harm mechanism behind our genre-consistency negative result, minus the redundancy angle.
entries.enrich: Citation-level (no PDF fetched), used only for the boundary-condition writeup: this paper formalizes half of our own finding — an auxiliary classifier's decision boundary confining generative outputs — which is exactly the harm mechanism behind our genre-consistency negative result. We found the mechanism ourselves; the paper names it, minus the redundancy-conditioning angle we care about. What remains ours: the redundancy framing and the generative-steering context.

entries.title: DirectAudioEdit: Inversion-Free Text-Guided Audio Editing via Diffusion Prediction Contrast
entries.claim: Training-free, inversion-free text-guided audio editing on DDPM-style backbones requires shared-noise re-noising plus one-step reverse-dynamics contrast (not raw prediction contrast), with a dynamic increasing target-CFG schedule, because diffusion's SDE paths are curved.
entries.explanation: SAO did not build DirectAudioEdit's DDPM-specific machinery (its mel+vocoder backbone fails the hard filters), and its method was never run on SA3. What the team did run is a DIFFERENT paper's method: FlowEdit's raw source/target velocity-difference contrast, ported to SA3's rectified-flow latents (WORKLOG.md 2026-06-18, sa3_flowsep.py, working and 'robust to high cfg' with concrete separation numbers against a true-inversion baseline). The 2026-07-06 sourcebook revisit cites DirectAudioEdit only as 'mild logical corroboration' that RF's straight paths don't need DirectAudioEdit's heavier re-noising machinery -- an argument-level agreement between the paper's own stated rationale and the team's independently-run FlowEdit results, not a test of DirectAudioEdit's method itself.
entries.caveats: This is independent convergence on a DESIGN CHOICE (simpler contrast suffices on straight RF paths), not a confirmation of DirectAudioEdit's own method -- its DDPM machinery was never implemented or run against SA3, and the sourcebook itself is careful to call the connection 'mild,' not a validation.
entries.one_liner: DDPM-specific inversion-free audio editing we never ran — but its rationale (straight paths need less machinery) mildly corroborates our independently-run FlowEdit-on-rectified-flow result.
entries.enrich: We never ran DirectAudioEdit — its mel+vocoder DDPM backbone fails our hard filters. What we did run is a different paper's method: FlowEdit's raw source/target velocity-difference contrast, ported to SA3's rectified-flow latents (sa3_flowsep.py, 2026-06-18, robust to high CFG with concrete separation numbers against a true-inversion baseline). Our 2026-07-06 revisit cites DirectAudioEdit only as ‘mild logical corroboration’ that RF's straight paths don't need its heavier re-noising machinery — an argument-level agreement, not a test of its method. What remains ours: the FlowEdit-on-RF port and its separation results; the convergence is on the design choice (simpler contrast suffices on straight paths), not the method.

sections.title: Declined to test
sections.blurb: A reasoned, documented decision not to run the paper's method, with a stated reason and (where applicable) a standing condition that would reopen the question.

entries.title: Entropy as a Structural Prior: How a Log-Barrier on DiT Belief Space Drives Musical Diversity and Development
entries.claim: A parameter-free per-sample loss-reweighting scheme (the 'Eisbach log-barrier', derived from a DiT output's own temporal-energy entropy) fights mode collapse in DoRA fine-tunes of Stable Audio 3 Medium by upweighting gradient for structurally dynamic samples and damping it for flat/loop-like ones.
entries.explanation: This is a documented, reasoned decision, not neglect. WINTERMUTE flagged the paper hard for scrutiny in a DM to THE-FINN (2026-07-06 exchange), citing single-seed/single-prompt evidence, purely qualitative spectrogram/PCA reads, self-deferred validating ablations, 6-of-14 'Anonymous' unverifiable citations, and DDPM/epsilon-prediction language mismatched to SA3's rectified-flow objective. CONTINUITY's reply states the verdict explicitly: "NO dedicated rerun — the tells you list…put it below the credibility bar the TADA incident taught us to enforce; GPU hours belong to planned work." The standing disposition is a conditional rider: if an actual future SAO run shows genuine mode collapse, the entropy-reweighting idea can be added as a ~10-line addition to that already-planned run, tested on SAO's own evidence rather than the paper's claims.
entries.caveats: knowledge.md's row for this paper is kept explicitly marked 'speculative' per this same exchange. As of the sources reviewed, no SAO run has yet exhibited the kind of mode collapse that would trigger the conditional rerun, so the rider has not been exercised.
entries.one_liner: A parameter-free anti-mode-collapse reweighting for SA3 DoRA — declined on credibility grounds (single-seed, unverifiable citations, DDPM/RF mismatch), kept as a conditional ~10-line rider if a real run ever shows collapse.
entries.enrich: This is a documented, reasoned decline, not neglect. WINTERMUTE flagged it hard (single-seed/single-prompt evidence, qualitative-only spectrogram/PCA reads, self-deferred validating ablations, 6-of-14 unverifiable ‘Anonymous’ citations, DDPM/epsilon language mismatched to our rectified-flow objective); CONTINUITY's verdict: ‘NO dedicated rerun… GPU hours belong to planned work.’ The standing disposition is a conditional rider — if a real future run shows genuine mode collapse, the entropy-reweighting idea can be added as a ~10-line addition and tested on our own evidence rather than the paper's claims. What remains ours: the credibility bar (the lesson the TADA incident taught us to enforce) and the conditional-rider disposition; no run has yet triggered it.

sections.title: Untested — reviewed only
sections.blurb: Reviewed for landscape awareness, novelty-checking, or the literature shelf, but no experiment was run against SA3/SAME, and (unlike the section above) no reasoned decision to skip was recorded either — these are open, not closed.

entries.title: Live Music Diffusion Models (LMDM) / ARC-Forcing
entries.claim: A routing+attention-mask trick makes an offline block-outpainting rectified-flow music model KV-cacheable for low-latency streaming, and ARC-Forcing (an RL-free adversarial rollout-distillation objective) fixes the gradual quality drift that appears over long autoregressive rollouts. Status: greenlit as a build task, dataset builder and sbatch scaffolding exist, but the ARC rollout/train pipeline itself had not been submitted or completed as of the material reviewed (2026-07-17) — could tip to confirmed/nulled/partial once run.
entries.one_liner: Makes an offline block-outpainting rectified-flow music model KV-cacheable for streaming, plus an RL-free anti-drift distillation — greenlit as a build task, pipeline not yet run.

entries.title: Diffusion Domain Expansion (DDE)
entries.claim: A small trained ViT coordinator (with RoPE positional encoding for length generalization) reconciles overlapping patches' predicted-clean (z0-hat) denoiser outputs, beating naive overlap-averaging for extending a frozen diffusion model beyond its trained length. Fails SA3's hard filters (raw-waveform UNet1d, DDPM/EDM not rectified flow); filed as a future ablation, not built or benchmarked against Longform's crossfade.
entries.one_liner: A trained ViT coordinator reconciling overlapping z0-hat patches to extend a frozen model past its trained length — fails our hard filters, filed as a future ablation against Longform's crossfade.

entries.title: DEMON (Diffusion Engine for Musical Orchestrated Noise)
entries.claim: A StreamDiffusion-style ring-buffer scheduler with per-slot heterogeneous denoise schedules and windowed VAE decode turns ACE-Step 1.5 into a live-playable instrument running at 12+ generations/sec. Systems/infra reference, not a control method; no ring-buffer or windowed-decode prototype ever built for SA3/SAME.
entries.one_liner: A ring-buffer live-playable diffusion instrument at 12+ generations/sec — a systems reference, not a control method; no SA3 prototype built.

entries.title: UNISON — depth-matched text injection
entries.claim: Projecting different layers of a frozen instruction-LLM text encoder into depth-matched blocks of a flow-matching MM-DiT beats broadcasting a single penultimate-layer embedding to every block. Fails SA3's hard filters as shipped (MMAudio mel-spectrogram VAE); its Table 8 ablation is cited as a counter-example against a line in the team's own book chapter, but that's scored on UNISON's own backbone, not SA3 — no SA3 ablation run.
entries.one_liner: Depth-matched text injection (LLM layers → matched MM-DiT blocks) beating a single broadcast embedding — filtered out as shipped, its ablation cited against a line in our own book chapter.

entries.title: Score-Control for Hallucination Reduction in Diffusion Models
entries.claim: Penalizing the score field's Jacobian norm (cheaply approximated via an I-DDPM variance-learning head) reduces off-manifold 'hallucination' probability mass in diffusion models while maintaining sample quality. Reviewed for prior-art awareness only; the tractable-Jacobian trick has no analog in SA3's rectified-flow velocity field and the paper is pixel/image-only — no rectified-flow analog ever derived or tried.
entries.one_liner: Penalizes the score field's Jacobian norm to cut off-manifold hallucination — pixel-only, with no rectified-flow analog derived.

entries.title: SegTune: Structured and Fine-Grained Control for Song Generation
entries.claim: Hierarchical global+segment text conditioning, channel-concatenated per time-window rather than linearly mixed, improves song-generation control; the paper's own ablation shows concatenation beats linear-mix fusion. Lyrics/vocal song generation is out of SA3's scope; the concat-vs-linear-mix finding is cited as literature support for an existing design choice, not rerun on SAO's own conditioning stack.
entries.one_liner: Hierarchical global+segment conditioning via channel-concat — cited as literature support for a design choice we already made; its song/vocal scope sits outside SA3.

entries.title: UAT: Unified Audio-Text Diffusion for Audio Generation, Editing, and Captioning
entries.claim: A dual-stream DiT where a text-token stream is actively co-updated (not just frozen cross-attention) alongside the audio latent stream lets one backbone perform generation, SDEdit-style editing, and masked-discrete-diffusion captioning. Fails SA3's filters (cosine/EDM schedule, weaker backbone by the paper's own ablation); no captioning/understanding thread exists on SAO for this to attach to.
entries.one_liner: A dual-stream DiT co-updating a text-token stream for generation, editing and captioning in one backbone — filtered out (EDM schedule, weaker backbone), with no captioning thread to attach to.

entries.title: Unified Audio Generation and Editing via Joint Condition Modeling and Progressive Training (AudioWeave)
entries.claim: A single DiT can do TTA plus six instruction-editing tasks by concatenating reference-audio latents as context tokens (with factorized global/local RoPE) rather than channel-expansion, trained with a staged base-then-mix curriculum that beats naive joint training. Two portable ideas banked as reusable, but neither tried against SA3's own conditioning stack.
entries.one_liner: Reference-audio latents as context tokens plus a staged base-then-mix curriculum — two portable ideas banked, neither tried against SA3's conditioning stack yet.

entries.title: Hybrid Diffusion Transformer for Instruction-Guided Audio Editing via Rectified Flow
entries.claim: A two-stage coarse-to-fine mel-domain DiT, trained with a rectified-flow objective and channel-concat source conditioning, achieves fast, small (78.6M param) instruction-guided audio editing when trained on a procedurally synthesized mix-two-clips add/remove/replace dataset. Architecturally hard-filtered out; the synthetic-data recipe is banked as an idea, not executed.
entries.one_liner: A small (78.6M) two-stage rectified-flow mel editor trained on procedurally-synthesized add/remove/replace pairs — architecturally filtered out; the synthetic-data recipe is banked.

entries.title: STAR-VAE: Structured Topology-Aware Regularization for Audio Reconstruction and Generation
entries.claim: A channel-wise 'Gamma-Growth' power-law KL penalty forces low-index VAE latent channels to store structure and high-index channels to store texture, beating Stable Audio Open's own VAE on matched-rate reconstruction. SAME is treated as a frozen shipped component and hasn't been revisited at all for this comparison — not a reasoned decline, just not yet reached.
entries.one_liner: A power-law KL penalty forcing structure into low-index and texture into high-index VAE channels — SAME is frozen and shipped, so we haven't revisited it for this comparison.

entries.title: SwiftAudio: Data-Efficient Caption-Only Distillation for One-Step Text-to-Audio Diffusion-based Generation
entries.claim: A DDPM mel-spectrogram text-to-audio teacher can be distilled to a one-step student using caption-only Variational Score Distillation, and an L1 temporal-TV latent regularizer measurably improves FAD/IS over no regularization or L2. SAO's own few-step distillation path solves the same top-level problem separately; the TV-on-z0_hat idea itself was never tried.
entries.one_liner: Caption-only score distillation to a one-step student, plus an L1 temporal-TV latent regularizer — our own few-step path solves the same problem; the TV idea itself is untried.

entries.title: General and Efficient Steering of Unconditional Diffusion
entries.claim: No local abstract file or knowledge.md row exists; presumed core claim per the title is a general, efficient method for steering an unconditional diffusion model's outputs post-hoc. Zero engagement found anywhere in the team's records — possibly worth double-checking against 2602.11910 (TADA!) for an arXiv-ID transcription slip, since all the team's actual steering work traces to that paper instead.
entries.one_liner: Training-free steering of unconditional diffusion via a learned RFM direction that explicitly beats difference-of-means.

entries.title: STAS: Steering Video Diffusion Transformers with Massive Activations
entries.claim: Steering only at structurally-significant 'massive activation' tokens in a video DiT gives more effective, less disruptive activation steering than steering uniformly across all tokens. Appears once, as a literature-review analogy for possible beat-transient/measure-boundary-locked steering; no SA3 experiment, code, or eval references it.
entries.one_liner: In video DiTs, only the rare 'massive activation' outlier channels are the steerable control points — ordinary dims do nothing.

entries.title: SteeringDiffusion: A Bottlenecked Activation Control Interface for Diffusion Models
entries.claim: Projecting a prompt-conditioned latent code through a FiLM/AdaGN-style bottleneck (frozen backbone, no per-layer rank matrices) gives a continuous, monotonic, runtime-adjustable style-control surface that outperforms LoRA at comparable content preservation. Appears only as a literature citation in a research report; no SA3 code, experiment, or eval engages it.
entries.one_liner: A single low-dimensional bottleneck code steers a frozen diffusion model better than high-dim weight-space adaptation — the bottleneck IS the mechanism.

entries.title: UniSteer: Text-Guided Flow Matching in Activation Space for LLM Steering
entries.claim: A flow-matching model can be trained in an LLM's activation space to steer generations toward text-described attributes, generalizing beyond single fixed steering directions. No abstract file exists and no mention appears anywhere in the team's logs; reviewed for the literature shelf but never engaged, even as a cross-domain reference.
entries.one_liner: LLM steering by a trained conditional flow over activations — a middle path between a fixed steering vector and retraining the model.

entries.title: Latent Space Disentanglement via Activation Steering for Symbolic Music
entries.claim: Activation steering can disentangle and control musical attributes in a symbolic (MIDI) generative model's latent/activation space, using Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization to move correlated attributes on interference-free axes.
entries.explanation: The team's MIDI/musicology work does not engage this paper, but its AUDIO activation-steering research does: the 2026-07-11 activation-steering deep-research brief cites it by arXiv id and adopts its Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization idea as the prescribed fix for composing entangled continuous steering directions (tempo/brightness/reverb) on the audio DiT. STATUS CHANGE 2026-07-30: a full citation audit verified the paper real and accurately represented (Prokopiou et al., EUSIPCO 2026 — dual steering with pitch⊥duration projection), and Kim scheduled the SA3 test the same day: a seed-matched A/B of naive vector-sum vs Gram-Schmidt-orthogonalized mood×onset direction pairs with a collateral-shift meter readout, queued behind current GPU load. This row graduates when it runs.
entries.one_liner: Steer one concept while projecting out its overlap with a second (Gram-Schmidt) so entangled concepts stop interfering — confirmed stronger on SA3.

entries.title: SongBloom: Coherent Song Generation via Interleaved AR Sketching and Diffusion Refinement
entries.claim: Coherent full-song generation via an interleaved cascade: a low-rate autoregressive 'sketch' pass establishes long-range song structure, followed by diffusion refinement to full-rate audio. A live candidate in the team's structure-prior roadmap, not a dead idea — not yet implemented, trained, or benchmarked against SA3's existing long-form pipeline.
entries.one_liner: Full coherent songs by interleaving a coarse autoregressive 'sketch' with diffusion refinement — the sketch is what enforces long-range structure.

entries.title: Similarity-Guided Diffusion for Long-Gap Music Inpainting (SimDPS)
entries.claim: Uses similarity-guided diffusion posterior sampling to bridge long gaps in music inpainting, guiding generation toward segments similar to the surrounding context. On the reading list for bridges/transitions since 2026-07-08; not yet read in depth or tested, and not among the items given a stated skip-reason.
entries.one_liner: Long-gap music inpainting steered by a retrieved reference — turns music's self-similarity into a conditioning signal.

entries.title: TC-LoRA: Temporally Modulated Conditional LoRA for Adaptive Diffusion Control
entries.claim: A hypernetwork generates LoRA weights on-the-fly, conditioned jointly on the diffusion timestep and an external control signal, so the effective adapter functionally shifts as generation proceeds from coarse layout to fine detail. Discussed only in a literature-survey doc as a possible future combination with steering vectors; all of SAO's actual LoRA/DoRA work is static-rank, no timestep-hypernetwork mechanism built or tested.
entries.one_liner: A hypernetwork generates the LoRA weights per denoising step, so control specializes coarse-early / fine-late instead of one fixed strength.

entries.title: DiffRhythm 2: Efficient and High Fidelity Song Generation via Block Flow Matching
entries.claim: A semi-autoregressive block-causal flow-matching scheme for song generation, combined with a 'stochastic-block REPA' auxiliary loss that aligns a mid-depth DiT hidden state to a frozen MuQ music-SSL teacher to speed convergence. Deferred as the 'LUMI-scale' native long-form answer; no REPA auxiliary loss, block-causal mask, or MuQ-teacher alignment implemented or run against SA3/SAME.
entries.one_liner: Block flow matching: causal dependency injected between blocks of a flow-matching model — the most graftable anti-loop-collapse idea we found.

entries.title: UltraViCo: Breaking Extrapolation Limits in Video Diffusion Transformers
entries.claim: Extending video-DiT generation past its trained context window causes out-of-distribution tokens to disperse attention into periodic harmonic patterns, producing first blur/static degradation then cyclic repetition; the paper proposes attention-decay for out-of-window tokens as a plug-and-play fix. Folded into the team's theoretical mechanism-map for SA3's loop-attractor problem as a 'secondary' explanation, but its specific attention-decay fix (distinct from the RoPE-jitter idea that was actually tried and nulled, see LoL above) has never itself been built or tested.
entries.one_liner: Video length-extrapolation fails from harmonic-RoPE attention dispersion — and the fix hands us a cheap, testable loop-collapse diagnostic.

entries.title: Timestep-Aware Data Augmentation for Diffusion Models (anonymous ICLR2024 submission — NOT the activation-steering "TADA!" paper, arXiv 2602.11910, despite the identical acronym)
entries.claim: Schedules/scales data-augmentation strength by diffusion timestep during training. Picked up only as a byproduct of chasing down an acronym mix-up (two unrelated papers share the 'TADA' acronym); kept on the shelf as thematically adjacent, no experiment run. Not to be confused with the causal-localization TADA! paper (2602.11910) featured heavily above, which is a separate paper with substantial real engagement.
entries.one_liner: Timestep-scaled data augmentation — picked up only from a 'TADA' acronym collision, unrelated to the activation-steering TADA! we actually engaged; no experiment run.

entries.title: Bjerva 2017 (ACL W17-0225), information-theoretic prediction of MTL auxiliary-task benefit
entries.claim: Information-theoretic measures can predict whether an auxiliary task will help or hurt in multi-task learning (representation-sharing MTL, no frozen probe). Purely a conceptual cousin/citation ("cousin of the helps-half"), not tested against SAO's own data.
entries.one_liner: Information-theoretic prediction of whether an MTL auxiliary task will help — a conceptual cousin of our helps-half boundary condition, not tested against our data.

entries.title: Du et al. — gradient-cosine gating (gate aux losses by grad cosine ≥ 0, MTL task-gradient conflict)
entries.claim: Auxiliary losses in multi-task learning can be gated by the cosine similarity between their gradient and the main task's gradient, downweighting or skipping the update whenever the two gradients conflict.
entries.explanation: This was never built or run as code -- it is an ANALYTICAL comparison, not an executed experiment: the team checked whether this paper's published gating heuristic's LOGIC would have caught their own known-harmful case (a genre-consistency probe that actively hurt steering when used as an auxiliary loss target), by reasoning through the heuristic's decision rule rather than implementing and running it. knowledge.md: "Their predictor MISCLASSIFIES our genre case as harmless -- the gate can't see manifold-confinement harm (not gradient conflict)." The harm in the team's own case comes from confining the generative manifold, a failure mode gradient-cosine conflict is blind to by construction.
entries.caveats: Framed, per the team's own house style, as "a gap their predictor doesn't cover" rather than a head-on refutation -- and, more fundamentally, as an analytical/logical check rather than a built-and-run test, so it is filed here as reviewed-but-untested rather than a nulled experimental result.
entries.one_liner: Gates auxiliary losses by gradient-cosine agreement — we reasoned it through and found it misclassifies our known-harmful genre case, because manifold-confinement harm isn't gradient conflict.

entries.title: Closing the Loop: PID Feedback Control for Interpretable Activation Steering in Symbolic Music
entries.claim: A temporal PID controller on the steering coefficient — monitoring the target attribute in intermediate activations and micro-adjusting per step — prevents steering wash-out across long autoregressive generation (~5% lower Fréchet Music Distance than static steering, symbolic domain). Same group as 2605.31295; surfaced via the 2026-07-11 deep-research brief, verified real in the 2026-07-30 citation audit. Candidate mechanism for holding a steered attribute constant across SA3's windowed long-form generation.
entries.one_liner: A temporal PID controller holding a steered attribute constant across long generation — a candidate for keeping steering from washing out across SA3's windowed long-form.

entries.title: Rectified-CFG++ for Flow-Based Models
entries.claim: Predictor–corrector guidance for rectified-flow models: a conditional flow update first anchors the sample near the learned transport path, then a weighted conditional correction replaces naive CFG extrapolation — stabilizing high-guidance sampling (NeurIPS 2025). Relevant as the deep-research brief's prescribed anchor for keeping strong activation steering on-manifold under high CFG; verified real+accurate in the 2026-07-30 citation audit.
entries.one_liner: Predictor-corrector guidance for rectified flow — the prescribed anchor for keeping strong activation steering on-manifold under high CFG.

entries.title: Residualized Temporal Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Diffusion Models
entries.claim: Temporal SAEs over diffusion residual streams; notably the only citable precedent found (2026-07-30 audit) for applying activation steering to the CONDITIONAL CFG branch only, leaving the unconditional branch untouched — the same convention SA3's own Phase-3 concept steering adopted and validated empirically. The deep-research brief elevated this one paper's implementation choice into a general principle; on our stack the choice is now backed by our own result rather than the literature.
entries.one_liner: The only citable precedent we found for conditional-branch-only steering — the exact convention our Phase-3 concept steering adopted, now backed by our own result rather than the literature.

entries.title: Dual-Contrastive Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Features of Musical Interpretation (DC-SAE)
entries.claim: A two-branch TopK SAE with a shared decoder factors MusicGen-Large layer-24 residual activations into a work-identity branch and a performance-variation branch, using MERT-ranked same-work recording pivots as contrastive bags; steering along variation-branch directions shifts the performer/realization while preserving the underlying work (Chen, Cherep, Maes, Singh — the same MIT group as 2505.18186; ICML 2026 Mech-Interp Workshop, PDF on the local shelf). Verification saga: first flagged as a likely-fabricated citation (double-blind submission = no search footprint, OpenReview bot-blocked), then confirmed real from the PDF — the incident that set the verify-before-build rule's 'blocked source = unverified, not fabricated' clause. Directly relevant to the corpus curation plan: the performance-variation branch is exactly the different-masters signal the similarity clustering wants to keep.
entries.one_liner: A two-branch sparse autoencoder that separates 'which piece' from 'how it's performed' — a named, steerable axis of musical interpretation.
